premise: I used my late husband’s $85,000 life insurance to launch a hand‑poured candle company with my daughter‑in‑law, notarizing a 50/50 partnership and a lifetime candle subscription; after a national home‑décor chain offered $520,000 for the scent formulas and inventory, she forged a dissolution, sold the brand, and sent me a $2,800 “thank‑you” candle. I discovered the original agreement tucked inside a wax mold, voided the sale, and now run “Wick of Deceit Candles” — she wicks jars in an apron that says “Snuffed Out Trust,” and every candle bottom prints her perjury docket.
